note: After Hill's original English description of 1915 (new species Heterotermes validus sp. nov.); the passage covered here is the alate (winged form) only, the soldier and worker being described on later pages of the same work and not included. The measurements are single values.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: New species (sp. nov.); the form read here is the alate. Body ochraceous yellow; head large, longer than wide, rounded behind; frons projecting and flat, separated from the back of the head by a broad arcuate suture which runs in front of the compound eye and extends backward to the level of the posterior margin of the compound eye; a small circular tubercle in the middle of the head, on the same line as the posterior margin of the compound eye; ocelli absent; antennae very short, 16-segmented.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Body overall ochraceous yellow, the legs and antennae paler; wings pale smoky brown tinged with ochre, the veins smoky brown; postclypeus pale yellow; labrum pale ferruginous. Body length (to the tip of the abdomen) 4.5 mm, to the wing tips 10 mm. Head large, longer than wide, rounded behind; frons projecting and flat, separated from the back of the head by a broad arcuate suture which passes in front of the compound eyes and extends backward to the same line as the posterior margin of the eyes; a small circular tubercle in the middle of the head, on the same line as the posterior margin of the compound eyes. Postclypeus large, posterior margin arched, the sides slightly rounded, the front truncate, divided into two lobes by a deep suture, the posterior lobe convex with an indistinct suture along the midline. Labrum long and convex, widest at the base, sloping towards the truncate apex, not reaching the tip of the mandibles. Compound eyes small, circular, coarsely faceted and projecting, on the sides of the head, equidistant from the tip of the labrum and the posterior margin of the head. Ocelli absent. Antennae very short, 16-segmented, inserted in circular pits in front of the compound eyes: segment 1 longest, segment 2 about half as long and slender, segment 3 very small, segments 3—10 fused, segments 11—13 moniliform, segments 14—16 hairy. Thorax with scattered hairs.
